method: Review 35 pending phrases and add narrowly scoped receptive support for remaining barriers. Consent, coercion and speaker uncertainty are retained; no graphic practice or unsupported inference of rescue is added.
phrases: as per her lawsuit
according to what her lawsuit states
根据她的诉状所述
As per the written request, we sent a copy by email.
按照书面请求，我们通过电子邮件发送了一份副本。
As per is formal and often bureaucratic; according to is more natural in everyday speech. Source attributes the claim to the filing, not to this reviewer.
figure out
understand or find a solution to something
弄明白；想出办法
I'm trying to figure out why the printer stopped.
我正想弄明白打印机为什么停了。
Separable with pronouns: figure it out. Here it is about understanding college life, not numerical calculation.
legal drinking age
the minimum age at which drinking alcohol is legally permitted in the relevant setting
法定饮酒年龄
The sign asks visitors to confirm that they are of legal drinking age.
标牌要求来访者确认自己已达到法定饮酒年龄。
Of legal drinking age is the natural eligibility phrase. No jurisdiction-wide age rule or exception is asserted by this language example.
go off campus
leave the university campus grounds
离开校园；去校外
We often go off campus for lunch.
我们经常去校外吃午饭。
Go off campus is movement outside campus, not leaving university permanently. The source's Subaru/Uber wording remains separately flagged.
not associated with
not connected or affiliated with a person or organization
与……没有关联；不隶属于……
The club is not associated with the company.
这个俱乐部与那家公司没有隶属或关联关系。
Associated with describes a relationship; source may be distinguishing school affiliation from employment, so it should not be generalized into no connection of any kind.
not even former members
not people who belonged to the group in the past, despite that possibility being expected
甚至连以前的成员也不是
Some advisers are not even former members of the club.
有些顾问甚至连该俱乐部以前的成员也不是。
Even emphasizes the surprising absence of a prior-membership link. Source says sometimes, not that every employee has this background.
around 10 p.m.
at approximately ten o'clock at night
晚上十点左右
We expect to arrive around 10 p.m.
我们预计晚上十点左右到达。
Around is approximate, p.m. marks after noon. This is an event-time phrase from the account, not a verified audio timestamp.
at least from the filing
limiting an inference to what can be understood from the filed document
至少从诉讼文件来看
At least from the report, the problem appears limited.
至少从报告来看，问题似乎范围有限。
The teaching example substitutes report. Source restricts the evidentiary basis and does not prove a venue served no alcohol under all circumstances.
by this point
by the stage already reached in the account
到这个时候；截至这一步
By this point, we had finished the first draft.
到这个时候，我们已经完成了初稿。
By highlights an accumulated state. Source drink count remains approximate and self-reported; no precise quantity is verified.
meet up with
meet someone by arrangement, usually socially
与……见面；和……碰头
I'll meet up with Maya after work.
我下班后会和玛雅碰头。
Informal arranged meeting, not necessarily first acquaintance. Source fragment states purpose and belongs with the preceding movement.
according to the lawsuit
as stated in the lawsuit
根据诉状所述
According to the lawsuit in the exercise, the payment was never received.
根据练习中的诉状所述，款项一直没有收到。
Legal-source attribution, not a finding of truth. Teaching example is fictional and unrelated to the podcast allegations.
at this point
at the particular stage being discussed
在这个时候；到了这个阶段
At this point, we need to pause and check the figures.
到了这个阶段，我们需要暂停并核对数字。
At locates the stage; by this point often emphasizes what has accumulated before it. Source's capacity claim remains attributed.
eventually comes back
returns after some time or intervening events
过了一阵终于回来；后来回来
The character eventually comes back to apologize.
那个角色后来回来道歉。
Eventually is after a period, not possibly. The fictional teaching motive is not supplied to the source participant.
it appears that
it seems from available information that something is true
看来似乎……
It appears that the appointment has been moved.
看来预约似乎改了时间。
A cautious inference, not a guarantee. Keep appears in source rather than turning the account into certainty.
leads her upstairs
guides or takes her to a higher floor
领她上楼
The receptionist leads her upstairs to the meeting room.
接待员领她上楼去会议室。
Upstairs is an adverb without to. Leading a person somewhere does not itself show consent to unrelated later actions.
leaves her alone
leaves her without the speaker's or another person's company
把她独自留下；让她单独待着
He leaves her alone to finish the puzzle.
他让她独自把拼图完成。
Source says alone with another person, meaning the first person departs, not that nobody remains. Distinguish leave someone alone meaning stop bothering them.
on the couch
seated or positioned on a sofa
在沙发上
The documents are on the couch.
文件在沙发上。
Use on for a seat surface. Couch is a sofa, not coach; the phrase does not describe the uncertain plopped up wording elsewhere.
three to five minutes
a duration ranging from three minutes to five minutes
三到五分钟
The download usually takes three to five minutes.
下载通常需要三到五分钟。
To connects lower and upper bounds. Source attributes this estimate to one person and explicitly questions the actual duration.
as alleged
as claimed, without treating the claim itself as proof
据指称；如所指控的那样
The damage occurred during delivery, as alleged in the complaint.
投诉中指称，损坏是在运输期间发生的。
Alleged preserves evidentiary status; it does not imply the allegation is necessarily false. The example is a generic complaint, not a podcast quotation.
has never done
has not performed or experienced an activity before the reference time
此前从未做过或经历过……
She has never done this kind of presentation before.
她以前从未做过这种演示。
Present perfect plus never describes prior experience. Done + drug names can mean used a substance in informal speech; no drug-use instructions are supplied.
nobody locks it
no person locks the thing already mentioned
没有人把它锁上
The shared cupboard is open; nobody locks it.
共用柜子一直开着，没有人把它锁上。
It refers to the room/door in source. Unlocked does not automatically mean anyone has permission for every action inside.
passing around
handing something from one person to another
传递；轮流传看或传用
They were passing around a sign-up sheet.
他们正在传递一张报名表。
Separable: pass it around. Source's nested Jane says they said keeps the substance identification as a reported claim.
soon after
a short time following the preceding event
不久之后
Soon after the meeting, she sent a summary.
会议结束不久，她就发了一份摘要。
Relative timing, not an exact interval. Source introduces alleged acts and does not supply a precise duration.
without her consent
without her freely given agreement or permission
未经她同意
The photo was shared without her consent.
照片未经她同意就被分享了。
Consent is agreement, not mere presence or failure to speak. Source explicitly alleges absence of consent; that attribution is retained.
according to the sequence
following the order presented in an account
按照所述的顺序来看
According to the sequence in the report, testing came before approval.
按照报告中的顺序，测试发生在批准之前。
Usually complete with of events or an identified account. The source's temporary hope about a person's motives is not established by event order.
at some point
at an unspecified time or stage
在某个时候；到了某个阶段
At some point, we'll need to review the plan.
到了某个阶段，我们需要重新审视计划。
Deliberately leaves the time unspecified; no exact audio timing or event time may be inferred.
falls asleep
begins sleeping
睡着
The child falls asleep during the ride.
孩子在乘车途中睡着了。
Fall asleep is entering sleep; be asleep is the state. Source does not establish why the person slept.
keeps trying to
continues making attempts to do something
不断尝试；一直试图……
She keeps trying to open the old file.
她一直试图打开那个旧文件。
Keep + -ing followed by try to + base verb. Repeated attempts do not imply success; source alleges continued unwanted attempts.
meanwhile
at the same time as another event
与此同时
I prepared the slides; meanwhile, my colleague checked the data.
我准备幻灯片，与此同时，同事核对数据。
Connects concurrent strands, not necessarily a causal relationship. Source's according to the lawsuit still scopes the following allegation.
figure out college
learn how to navigate the demands and routines of college life
摸索适应大学生活
She's still trying to figure out college and living away from home.
她还在摸索如何适应大学生活和离家独立生活。
College is the experience to navigate, not a puzzle with one answer. Informal broad object after figure out; transferable to figure out a new job.
get hired
be selected for paid employment
被雇用；获得聘用
He hopes to get hired by a local company.
他希望被一家本地公司聘用。
Conversational get-passive; getting hired is not the same as joining an organization as a student member.
start dancing
begin moving rhythmically to music
开始跳舞
They start dancing when the music begins.
音乐一响，他们就开始跳舞。
Start + -ing or start to dance. Source has on the main room, an unusual preposition left unchanged; dancing is not consent to other acts.
sitting on the couch
being seated on a sofa
坐在沙发上
We were sitting on the couch discussing our plans.
我们坐在沙发上讨论计划。
Sit doubles t before -ing. Source's I guess marks a conjectural description, not verified observation.
pulls Jane off to the side
draws Jane away from the main group to one side
把简拉到一旁
She pulls her colleague off to the side for a quick question.
她把同事拉到一旁，简短地问了个问题。
Pull someone off to the side can describe steering someone aside; the phrase alone does not settle the amount of force. Names in the source remain unchanged.
a separate room
a different room apart from the one previously mentioned
另一间房；分开的房间
We used a separate room for the interview.
我们用了另一间房进行面试。
Separate is an adjective here, with an unstressed final syllable, not the verb meaning divide. Does not imply the room was private or locked.
Supposed to
expected or required to do or be something
应该；按职责应当……
The coordinator is supposed to help new members.
协调员按职责应该帮助新成员。
Be supposed to + verb; the fragment omits be because it continues the prior description. Indicates expected responsibility, not verified performance.
stamp
press a mark onto a surface using a stamp
盖印；盖章
Staff stamp each ticket at the entrance.
工作人员在入口给每张票盖印。
Verb of marking here, not a postage-stamp noun or stamping a foot. X's means X-shaped marks; giant is emphatic size description.
Hawaii themed
organized around images or ideas associated with Hawaii
以夏威夷为主题的
The invitation describes a Hawaii-themed event.
邀请函把活动描述为以夏威夷为主题。
Use -themed after a theme word and a hyphen in edited prose. The phrase does not verify cultural authenticity or alter the narrated event date.
capable of consenting
having the capacity to give meaningful agreement
具备作出有效同意的能力
The training discusses what it means to be capable of consenting.
培训讨论了具备作出有效同意的能力意味着什么。
Capable of + -ing; source alleges incapacity in a particular situation. This language note does not make a clinical or legal capacity determination.
plied plaintiff with
repeatedly supplied or pressed the plaintiff to take something
不断向原告提供或劝其接受……
The host plied the visitors with offers of tea.
主人不断向来访者劝茶。
Ply someone with something suggests persistent supply or urging. The neutral example teaches the construction without reproducing the alleged substance administration.
engaging in
taking part in an activity
从事；参与
The group is engaging in a discussion.
小组正在参与讨论。
Formal engage in + activity. Source sexual acts means sexual activity, and all without her consent denies voluntary agreement; engaging in does not itself imply consent.
reach for
extend a hand toward something to try to take or touch it
伸手去拿或触碰
She reached for the folder on the shelf.
她伸手去拿架子上的文件夹。
For marks the target of an attempt, not successful contact. Source alleges repeated unwanted attempts, with attribution preserved.
private parts
a polite or indirect term for genital areas
私处（委婉说法）
The safety lesson explains the term private parts respectfully.
安全课程以尊重的方式解释“私处”这个词。
Receptive euphemism, not an ordinary ownership phrase. Source's down there reinforces the same anatomical reference without adding detail.
swatting
making a quick striking movement to hit or brush something away
快速拍打；挥手拍开
She was swatting a fly away from the food.
她正挥手把一只苍蝇从食物旁赶开。
Quick striking/warding-off motion, not generic pushing. Source describes resistance to unwanted contact; teaching example uses an insect.
grabs
takes hold of suddenly or firmly
突然抓住；一把抓住
He grabs the rail when the bus stops.
公交车停下时，他一把抓住扶手。
Physical hold, not a rescue motive. Source's grabs Jane from Jonathan indicates a change in who holds her; later narration explicitly undermines the hoped-for rescue interpretation.
segments: Expected-role construction and caretaker meaning are linked. The fragment continues the previous subject, and kind of softens the characterization rather than proving the duties were performed.
Stamp is the marking action, X's names the shapes and both hands specifies placement. Giant is emphatic size description; no actual service or legal compliance is inferred.
The reusable theme construction is explained. Interesting choice is the narrator's aside about the date, not a factual correction or additional event.
Capacity construction and temporal/attribution markers are explicit. So drunk, she's ... is a spoken result construction; the claim remains in the lawsuit, not a capacity judgment by the lesson.
Persistent-supply construction now complements the role and alcohol-strength vocabulary. Believed to be qualifies identification, and the filing remains the source of the claim.

Formal activity construction, temporal sequence, legal-party labels and explicit absence of agreement are all explained. Sexual acts is defined receptively in the card note without adding graphic detail.
Concurrent timing, repeated attempts, directed hand movement and the euphemistic body reference are taught; the interrupted attribution still scopes the allegation.
Quick warding-off strikes are distinguished from pushing away; the source describes resistance rather than assent.
Sudden firm holding and the from-person construction are explained. Jane alleges preserves attribution; no rescue motive is inferred from the action.
The previously reviewed purpose connector explains the alleged reason for grabbing. It states links back to the filing, and kissing does not imply agreement to other contact.
